text:
John Carlson is 36, on a two-year deal with Tampa Bay after a long career in Washington, and he's playing like he knows exactly what the Lightning signed him for. He has 21 points in 23 games, 13 of them in his last ten, and CBS Sports counted ten points in one five-game run. He even had three assists against the Capitals on Nov. 17.

The process backs it up. With him on the ice at five on five, Tampa has taken 60% of the expected goals, the share of quality chances, 6.1 points better than without him. The part that won't last is the shooting: seven goals on 4.4 expected, 12% after 9% last season. Our range for his scoring rate is 1.8 to 2.5 points per 60, below the 2.8 he's running at, so expect the pace to ease without the role changing.

Evolving-Hockey had him 17th among defensemen last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged the weak spot: only 31% of his exits kept possession. Watch how he handles a heavy forecheck; that's where teams will test him.
